# Native cover presentation: exact admitted interfaces

2026-11-12. Constructive CLASSICAL surface comparator. This note records two
independently reviewed bridges. Native atlas, actual normalized frame and
downstream coordinate reconstruction remain separate until proved.

## Unmarked level cover from a supplied bounded Jacobian atlas

Fix fibre genus a and atlas type tau: projective ambient dimension, equation
count/degree, complete addition chart count/bidegree. Supply the actual
RADICAL ideal on every affine patch, identity, and coefficient t-degree T
and logarithmic height B over Q(t). Promise full geometric Sp_(2a)(F_ell)
monodromy for odd prime ell and the original principal polarization.

Then an unmarked splitting cover over Q(zeta_ell)(t), its ordered torsion
basis coordinates, base map, and deck generators have a deterministic
construction with degree, logarithmic height, bit cost and dense output
bounded by (2+ell+B+T)^C_tau. No family-dependent fixed-curve constant or
unpaid t-degree is hidden in the bound. Review:
audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-level-cover.md.

Expanded binary multiplication charts use the SAME parent chart for both
arguments of doubling. O(log ell) levels give polynomial counts/degrees/
heights in numerical ell. Impose identity cross-products for ALL charts;
completeness and etaleness of [ell] produce the reduced torsion scheme.
Pila's fixed-variable membership bound gives an explicit polynomial-size
coefficient matrix whose kernel/intersections construct the finite algebra.
Ratios of its minors bound t-degrees and heights in characteristic zero.

Take the fixed tensor power for ordered bases and exclude all nonzero
linear relations by support idempotents in the ORIGINAL algebra. A bounded
primitive-element search and cyclotomic/LLL-Hensel factorization then produce
components. Any basis generates the same splitting field. Over the cyclotomic
base, arithmetic image is contained in Sp and contains geometric Sp, hence
equals it; each component degree is |Sp|. Deck maps are computed by changing
the basis and testing the defining factor, with one common coefficient field.

The invariant alternating form is recovered only up to E=cB. ONE certified
nonzero Weil-pairing value fixes c and normalizes the universal frame. This
marking scalar is not a permission to choose the arithmetic Frobenius scalar.
Radicality is substantive: z²=0 cannot replace z=0 just because geometric
point sets agree. Fixed-variable elimination is valid only at the fixed fibre
genus; the auxiliary cover genus grows and requires separate algorithms.

## Native bounded atlas for the actual genus-31 fibre

The atlas input is now constructed for a smooth complete intersection
(5,3) in P3 over Q(t), with FIXED ambient/projective/parameter degree and
coefficient bit size B. The independent proof and advisory-report
dispositions are in audits/reviews/2026-11-12-native-jacobian-atlas.md;
the parent checked the complete proof and actual Anderson source.
Output type/degrees are format constants, coefficient heights O(B+1),
and bit cost polynomial in B. No rational curve point or field extension
is supplied. The constants are enormous; no practical claim follows.

A fixed resultant grid chooses a basepoint-free degree-15 hyperplane
pencil. At most90 values ramify. Among0,...,1875 choose1786 etale closed
fibres: five form reduced E of degree75, the other1781 give an evaluation
algebra of degree26715. Here n=h0(E)=45. The complete-intersection Koszul
resolution computes every needed RR space L(kE) by fixed-size linear
algebra; a finite-etale trace pairing supplies Anderson's compression
functional over Q(t) for ALL divisor classes simultaneously.

The source's abeliant is an integral universal polynomial of degree2n.
Every Jacobi discriminant has per-slot poles <=(8n-4)E, total26700.
Evaluation at26715 geometric points is therefore injective for every
discriminant. Tensor the CLOSED evaluation algebra rather than splitting
its support, apply every source permutation formula, and expand its
coefficients in a Q(t)-basis. At every pair each split component is zero
or on the SAME correct sum line, so every nonzero coefficient vector is
a valid addition law and these vectors cover EVERY geometric pair.
One explicit addition bidegree is(28350,28350).

Raw Jacobi equations are not assumed radical. Fixed-format elimination,
generic finite-algebra trace radical, contraction and saturation produce
the true radical projective ideal. A Poincare-family construction over an
algebraic closure gives an actual morphism Pic0->J_red; the complete atlas
makes J_red a smooth group variety. Proper bijectivity in characteristic
zero then gives an isomorphism, which descends by its naturality. A
geometric basepoint used in this proof is NOT an algorithmic input.

This pays the native atlas for this fixed-format family only. It does
not pay growing-genus auxiliary-cover normalization, arbitrary special
fibres/primes, normalized Weil pairing, or arithmetic reconstruction.
The genuine pairing/frame obligation remains in the native-completion
dispatch. Polynomial torsion-cover presentation follows by composing
with the supplied-atlas theorem under its full-monodromy promise.

## Arithmetic action from a genuine full similitude-frame scheme

Now supply the GENUINE frame torsor with evaluation into the original
L=J_fibre[ell]=R1 f_*mu_ell over Fq, with full geometric Sp monodromy and
nontrivial transvection inertia at r punctures. All presentation sizes are
charged. Gamma=GSp_n(F_ell), N=F_ell^n constant, S=N^vee. A frame is
(c,zeta), e(cu,cv)=zeta^(u^T Jv), with RIGHT action

    (c,zeta).g=(c g,zeta^lambda(g)).

Evaluation identifies the associated sheaf T x^Gamma N with the ACTUAL L.
All right deck maps commute with arithmetic Frobenius; N being constant does
not make L constant. Cartan--Leray on the disconnected torsor has H0 a
permutation module. Shapiro and central -I kill its group-cohomology
obstructions. Norm-zero transvection inertia makes the compact Hom equal
the OPEN cohomology Hom, not the parabolic part. Hence

    Hom_Gamma(N^vee,H1(C_full,mu_ell)) = H1(U,L)(1),
    dim = (r-2)n.

Independent review: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-full-similitude.md.
Apply q^-1 to the output matrix for arithmetic Frobenius on H1(U,L), or
q^-2 for L'=R1 f_*F_ell. Geometric Frobenius is the inverse matrix.
Do not confuse Galois action on divisors with inseparable morphism pullback.

Write A(g)=R_g^* (LEFT), P(g)=(R_g)_*=A(g^-1) (RIGHT). On one component
W0=Hom_Sp(S,J_C0[ell]), the exact pushforward equations and operator are

    phi g^T=P(g)phi,
    F_W(phi)=P(g_q^-1) sigma_q phi g_q^T,  lambda(g_q)=q.

Changing g_q by any Sp element, including -I, cancels exactly; no unknown
scalar survives. The transformed origin must be included on BOTH divisor
parts. Other cyclotomic components are DECK TRANSLATES, not necessarily
Frobenius conjugates; one component's zeta is sufficient for that reason.

The native-module algorithm applies over ONE field: first cyclotomic degree
ord_ell(q), then the charged regular-fibre avoidance extension and ONE
residue point of degree<=|Sp|, then the universal primary-killing extension.
Full primary multiplicities and pairing rank certify completeness. Costs
remain poly_(n,r)(ell, NUMERICAL P, presentation size, log1/eta), not polylogP.
No support splitting or lcm of separately chosen component fields is used.

Falsifiers include wrong torsion/frame dimensions, failed deck identities,
incorrect pushforward convention, failed exact Frobenius transport, or
omitted factors of the full frame fibre. A single factor's constant field
does not certify full geometric monodromy. Genuine native frame/evaluation,
inertia promises, parabolic filtering, arithmetic model, heights and
reconstruction are still required. No complete comparator or separation
follows from these two interfaces alone.

# Native small-characteristic natural torsion-module extraction

2026-11-12. Parent construction independently reviewed and source-checked.
Review: audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-native-module.md. This removes a
specific supplied-module input in the repaired surface filter; no full native
point count, uniform height, novelty or separation claim.

## Contract and source scope

Fix n,r and odd prime ell. Supply an explicit geometrically connected compact
G=Sp_n(Fell) cover C/P1 with nontrivial transvection inertia at r geometric
punctures, in a separable plane/function-field model. Numerical degree, genus g,
map coordinates and finite-field presentation are charged; in the intended
surface construction they are polynomial inell at fixed n,r. Ground field is
Fq of characteristic P prime toell|G|. Deck generators are supplied over an
explicit charged finite field; a common field for the fixed O(n²) generators
costs at most their fixed-number product. Their minimum common definition
degree also has the bound |AutG|<=|G|^(n+n²), from Frobenius action on deck maps.
Do not take an arbitrary lcm of all separately given map coefficient fields.

Let V=J_C[ell](Fqbar)=H1(Cbar,muell), S=M* natural dimensionn, and
W=Hom_G(S,V). The CLOSED geometric lemma gives m=dimW=(r-2)n. This is the
OPEN-cohomology multiplicity, not the false parabolic stopping target.
No torsion basis, zeta numerator, target eigenvalues or splitting field is advice.

Output: a complete basis of W by rational torsion divisors over ONE explicit
common constant field; the geometric natural isotypic span E and genuine
q-power arithmetic Frobenius on E. The divisors are rational closed-place/ideal
representations; individual geometric support points need not all be rational.
That is sufficient for the RR/Kummer finite filter. If the intended output is
the separate multiplicity-space matrix F_W, the coefficient-module arithmetic
linearization A must be specified/constructed: F_W(phi)=F_q phi A^-1. The
cover's normalizer automorphism alone gives A only up to scalar. This convention
is an actual unresolved input when recovering an ORIGINAL family coefficient
system; choosing an arbitrary intertwiner is not genuine Frobenius advice paid.
With a coefficient module explicitly constant over the working base, A=I
for that base's Frobenius. Making only the deck maps constant is insufficient.
To output F_q on E, certify preservation of the natural representation under
the computed deck automorphism alpha(g)=F_q g F_q^-1: solve
A rho_S(g)=rho_S(alpha(g)) A and verify invertibility, or directly verify
F_q(E)=E in the computed complete space. An arbitrary abstract normalizer
assertion is not this certificate. Failure leaves W and V_small complete but
does not justify a restricted F_E or original-family multiplicity action.

Expected cost poly_(n,r)(ell, NUMERICAL P, presented bits,log1/eta). This is NOT
polylogP. Strongest baseline is the existing classical Couveignes torsion
algorithm, completed by small-characteristic zeta computation; no quantum step.

Primary sources actually read: Couveignes0706.0272 Sections6-8 and Theorem1
(smooth model, degree-one divisor and zeta required; strict-subgroup failure
permitted), plus Lauder--Wan published MSRI44 (2008) Theorems1/37 and the
Corollary3 proof pp610-611. The latter computes the zeta of a plane curve in
poly(degree,NUMERICAL P,logq), with no nonsingularity premise, and extracts the
smooth-model numerator by removing weight-zero factors. Actual source files:
audits/sources/surface_module_2026/{couveignes,lauder_wan_published}.{pdf,txt},
with provenance JSON. The separate author PDF is scanned; the published PDF
is the text source used here. Kozen local resolution and classical RR source
costs are reused from SURFACE_CLASSICAL_HEIGHT_UNIFORMITY.md.

## Simpler common-field construction

1. Work over a charged extension k0=F_(q^b) containing the deck generators
and an actual rational point O of C. Obtain O from ONE closed place above a
regular fibre of the separable degree-D map toP1: avoid denominators and
discriminant over a field larger than their degree, factor the fibre, and adjoin
ONE residue field of degree<=D. No whole irreducible fibre or common support
splitting field is required. Move that fibre to infinity if the RR source's
conventions require one rational infinite place. Normalization is charged by
Kozen. Compute the original smooth-model zeta numerator by Lauder--Wan;
derive extension zeta numerators by exact power sums/resultants. Coefficients
have O(g*b*h*logq+g) bits for extension degree b*h, a paid polynomial size.

2. Write F0=F_q^b. It commutes with G. Evaluation injects S tensor W into V
because S is absolutely simple and End_G(S)=Fell; its image is the semisimple
natural socle E, of dimensionn*m. This does NOT assume V semisimple or average
over G. On E, F0=I_S tensor B for some invertible m-dimensional B. Thus every
irreducible Frobenius factor on E has degree<=m, a fixed bound.

3. Factor chi_(F0) mod ell. Let a(X) be the product, with FULL multiplicities,
of every irreducible factor of degree<=m, and let b(X) be the remaining product.
Define V_small=ker a(F0), dimensionu=deg a. Include all such factors, not just
ones guessed to contain E. The reciprocal-twist partner lambda->q0/lambda
has the SAME irreducible degree, so V_small is closed under Weil duality and
the Weil pairing on it is nondegenerate. It contains E. It is G-stable because
F0 commutes with G, and is also stable under original F_q.

4. Put c=ceil(log_ell(max{1,2g})) and choose the explicit COMMON degree

    H=ell^c * product_(j=1..m)(ell^j-1).

This is polynomial inell andg for fixedm: ell^c<=ell*max{1,2g}, and the
semisimple product has fixed exponent. Every eigenvalue in V_small is killed
by a factor ell^j-1; ell^c kills EVERY ambient primary nilpotent block. Also
ell-1 dividesH, so muell lies in K=F_(q^(bH)). Thus V_small is fully rational
over this ONE field. No lcm over a growing collection of field degrees, no
full ambient torsion splitting and no small-target nilpotence shortcut.

5. Apply Couveignes Theorem1 over K, n_Couv=ell, with computed zeta, smooth
model and rational O. Verify every returned class is actual degree-zero
ell-torsion. Project returned classes by the CRT idempotent p(X) that is1
mod a and0 mod b. Coefficients inFell mean integer multiplication of divisor
classes; reduce divisors after each operation to degree-g effective D-gO.
All projected classes lie in V_small, even in a failed/strict-subgroup trial.
Build their Weil-pairing matrix, using a primitive ell-th root inK and a table
ofell powers for discrete logs. Accept a trial only if pairing rank=u.
This certifies the ENTIRE V_small, whose dimension is independently known
from chi. Select a nonsingular pairing minor as a basis. When Couveignes
succeeds on all rational torsion, this certificate necessarily succeeds.
A strict-subgroup output may pass only if it already contains V_small, which
is sufficient. Failed trials never certify absence.

6. Nondegenerate pairing gives exact coordinates of every deck/Frobenius image
in V_small. Optionally verify each reconstructed divisor equality by RR.
Solve the linear G-generator intertwiner equations to obtain Hom_G(S,V_small).
It equals W because E was contained in V_small; check dimensionm. Compute E
by the span of the n component classes of this Hom basis and restrict the
actual F_q action to E. A supplied genuine A gives F_W by composition; otherwise
return only F_E and the scalar ambiguity, not a falsely normalized W matrix.
Apply the preceding preservation certificate before making this restriction.
Frobenius acts on both parts: F_q(D-gO)=F_q(D)-gF_q(O); O need not be
F_q-rational. Reduce the resulting class back relative to O afterward.

7. Every returned divisor and coordinate identity has a checkable algebraic
certificate. Couveignes success>=1/2 plus an expected-polynomial subroutine
clock can be capped at a fixed multiple of its proved expected bound; retain
a constant joint success probability. Independent O(log1/eta) trials plus
finite-field subroutine error allocation produce bounded time and FAIL<=eta.
No unknown output is silently accepted, and no claim relies on semisimple
Frobenius. Exact exponent/clock constants come from the cited explicit
algorithms, not a finite numerical run.

## Report disposition boundary

OpenAI fast-surface-build completed, estimatedUSD2.268070. Its bounded-degree
primary/Weil-dual certificate and arithmetic-scalar warning motivate this
construction. Parent replaces its separate primary fields/target descent by
the single universal H above. Its optional prime-support representative lemma
and sharper output-field descent are UNNEEDED and not admitted here; closed
place representatives suffice. This avoids importing extra unverified claims.
The report supplied zeta; actual Lauder--Wan now pays it at numerical P cost.

Remaining upstream tasks: native G-cover construction and family coefficient
linearization, the already separate parabolic filter, characteristic-zero
lifting, uniform arithmetic/model heights and CRT recovery. No whole-paper
rehabilitation follows merely from this module. Cheapest falsifiers are the
field-degree bound, reciprocal duality, incomplete-output certificate or a
missing source input; no numerical experiment or quantum implementation is
needed for this exact construction. The independent review checks these
identities and the actual source prerequisites; no numerical control is needed.

# Numerical torsion lift from closed divisors

2026-11-12. Scoped classical bridge, independently source-checked in
`audits/reviews/2026-11-12-surface-mascot-lift.md`. This advances the native
surface comparator by paying numerical lifting once a faithful arithmetic
model is available. It does not pay reconstruction precision or that model.

## Exact statement

Given a genus-g curve with good reduction at P, an actual point O, a faithful
separable plane/function-field presentation of its good special curve, and
polynomial-size exact generic Riemann--Roch coordinates, an actual prime-to-P
ell-torsion class represented by closed divisors can be lifted to precision
P^E with polynomial bit cost in the presented sizes, g, numerical E, residue
extension degree, log P and log ell. No geometric support splitting is needed.
This is classical Mascot/Khuri-Makdisi arithmetic; no quantum advantage follows.

For d0=2g+1 and D0=d0 O, a class D-gO becomes D'=D+(d0-g)O,
represented by L(2D0-D'). Closed-place RR constructs this subspace. One common
residue field of polynomial degree supplies more than 5d0 evaluation points
away from denominators and exceptional loci: Hasse--Weil and factoring random
projection fibres give a polynomial capped clock. Unit derivatives lift them
over one unramified local extension. Their supports are independent of D.

Compute exact RR functions in a common-denominator normal form and saturate
their coefficient lattice. Faithful reduction and a nonzero reduced denominator
give independent reduced rational functions. Integrality of evaluations at
more than deg(D0) points forces genuine section integrality: a primitive
nonintegral section scaled into H0(D0) would otherwise have too many zeros
on the special curve. Nakayama then certifies the full integral RR lattice.
Use all products/constraints and full linear systems in the source's practical
randomized shortcuts; these variants remain polynomial.

At each precision-doubling step Mascot Algorithm10 lifts any Jacobian point
modulo P^e to P^(2e), then multiplies by N=0 mod P^e, N=1 mod ell. The error
lies in J_e/J_(2e), whose formal-group law is additive because the ideal is
square-zero; its exponent divides P^e. This proves unique torsion lifting,
including P=2, without the source's excessive global logarithm claim.

## Decisive corrections and remaining inputs

* Good reduction of the abstract curve alone is insufficient. Replacing y
  by Y=P y changes a good equation into Y²=P²f(x), with nonreduced displayed
  reduction. The faithful presentation and RR coordinate-size bound are
  explicit upstream obligations, not supplied by the words "good reduction".
* The source's blanket log:J1->P O^g isomorphism fails at two. On
  y²+xy=x³+4x+1, discriminant -4225, T=(-1/4,1/8) is nonzero 2-torsion
  reducing to O with formal parameter 2. The square-zero proof repairs the
  algorithm, not that assertion.
* Unique effective degree-g extraction requires residue h0(T+gO)=1.
  Its Abel differential then has zero kernel and cokernel by RR, so the
  divisor lifts with unit pivots, even with nonsplit or nonreduced support.
  Generic-characteristic-zero h0=1 alone is insufficient.
* Original Frobenius requires conjugation of O and the appropriate divisor
  correction. A row permutation needs the source's stable evaluation/base
  data. Numerical lift uniqueness does commute with arithmetic Frobenius.

The primary source is Mascot, arXiv:1808.03939, retained July2019 text,
Algorithms9/10, Theorem2.23 and Remark1.6:
`audits/sources/surface_module_2026/mascot_lift.{pdf,txt}`. Remark1.6 explicitly
leaves rational reconstruction uncertified without a height bound. The paid
`2026-11-12-closure-lift` call ended empty/truncated and supplies no evidence;
the independent source proof above is separately recorded.

Next decisive obligation: construct a faithful good auxiliary-prime model
and polynomial-size exact RR coordinates from the growing-degree native
cover, and bound canonical torsion coordinates. No full classical point count,
uniform reconstruction precision, speedup, hardness or separation is claimed.

97: Our strategy to compute ρ may be summarized as follows:
98: 
99:   1. Compute d points forming a basis of the image of Tρ in J(Fq )[`], where q = pa
100:      with a ∈ N large enough to split ρ (i.e. large enough that the points of the
101:      reduction of Tρ mod p are defined over Fq ),
102: 
103:   2. Fix an integer e ∈ N, and lift these points to approximations with accu-
104:      racy O(pe ) of `-torsion points in J(Qq ), that is to say to points of J(Zq /pe ),
105:      where Qq denotes the unramified extension of Qp whose residue field is Fq
106:      and Zq is the ring of integers of Qq ,
107: 
108:   3. Compute all the F` -linear combinations of these d points, thus obtaining a
109:      model of Tρ over Zq /pe ,
110: 
111:   4. Evaluate a rational map α : J 99K A1 defined over Q at these `d points, and
112:      form the monic polynomial F (x) whose roots are these values,
113: 
114:   5. Check that these values are distinct, else take another map from J to A1 and
115:      try again,
116: 
117:   6. Identify F (x) as a polynomial with coefficients in Q, or, if this fails, start over
118:      with a larger value of e.
119: 
120:    Indeed, for each nonzero t ∈ Tρ , α(t) lies in the field of definition Q(t) of t, so
121: the splitting field of F (x) is a subfield of the field corresponding to the kernel of ρ,
122: and agrees with it with high probability since most elements of a number field are
123: primitive elements. More precisely, a sufficient condition for the Galois action on
124: the roots of F (x) to reflect faithfully that on the points of Tρ is that α be injective
125: on Tρ , which is what we check at step 5.
126: 
127: Remark 1.5. In step 2, we are justified in speaking of J(Zq /pe ) thanks to our
128: assumption that C has good reduction at p.

130: Remark 1.6. Because of the identification performed at step 6, the output of this
131: algorithm is not guaranteed to be correct, and should be certified by methods such

134:     Throughout this algorithm, we use Kamal Khuri-Makdisi’s methods [KM04], [KM07]
135: to compute in J. We give a brief presentation of these techniques in section 2, in-
136: cluding a recipe to construct rational maps from J to A1 and comments on the
137: implementation over a p-adic field.
138:     The core of this article is devoted to the presentation of a technique to lift
139: torsion points from Fq to Qq (up to some arbitrary p-adic accuracy) in Makdisi’s
140: framework. After differential calculus preliminaries in section 3, we show how to lift
141: a point from J(Fq ) to J(Zq /pe ) for any e ∈ N in section 4, and then how to ensure
142: that the lift of an `-torsion point over Fq remains `-torsion over Zq /pe in section 5.
143:     Finally, we explain in detail how to use these tools to compute Galois represen-
144: tations in section 6, and we give explicit examples in section 7.
